name: Claude Portfolio

targets.name: Merck & Co.
targets.thesis: A steady drugmaker with strong earnings momentum; it is up 57% over 12 months, only 6% under its high, and its shares move less than most.
targets.risks: Uncertainty over the Keytruda patent cliff and US drug-pricing policy.

targets.name: Targa Resources
targets.thesis: A natural-gas pipeline and processing company whose fees grow with Permian volumes; it rose 12.6% this week and is close to its high.
targets.risks: A slowdown in Permian drilling, or weaker gas prices.

targets.name: Nucor
targets.thesis: The leading US steelmaker; tariffs protect it from imports and it has a strong balance sheet. It is up 71% over 12 months and still above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: Steel prices could fall back if industrial demand slows.

targets.name: CrowdStrike
targets.thesis: A leading cybersecurity company with strong recurring revenue; it rose 6% this week and is 32% above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: A high valuation that could fall further if software stocks sell off again.

targets.name: Marathon Petroleum
targets.thesis: A refiner that has profited from tight fuel supply and returns a lot of cash to shareholders; it rebounded 10% this week.
targets.risks: Refining margins could normalize after a record year.

targets.name: DuPont
targets.thesis: Since its breakup, the slimmer DuPont is being re-rated; the stock is up 17% in a month and above its 200-day average.
targets.risks: Problems from the separation or PFAS legal costs.

targets.name: Viatris
targets.thesis: A cheap generic-drug maker paying down debt; its momentum is strong and it is near its high.
targets.risks: Generic price erosion, or problems at its manufacturing sites.

targets.name: Valero Energy
targets.thesis: A low-cost refiner that returns a lot of cash to shareholders; it rose 9.7% this week.
targets.risks: Fuel demand could weaken or refining margins could shrink.

targets.name: NetApp
targets.thesis: A data-storage company exposed to AI demand at a reasonable valuation; results are due soon.
targets.risks: Weak guidance as the hardware selloff continues.

targets.name: Fortinet
targets.thesis: Network security with high profit margins and a cash-rich balance sheet; after a deep drawdown the valuation is more reasonable.
targets.risks: The firewall upgrade cycle could slow further and keep revenue growth weak.

targets.name: Morgan Stanley
targets.thesis: Wealth management gives steady fees, and dealmaking is recovering; the stock is up 5.4% this month.
targets.risks: Weaker markets would hurt trading and deal fees.

targets.name: Keysight Technologies
targets.thesis: A test-and-measurement company benefiting from AI and networking spending; it bounced 9.6% before results expected around November 23.
targets.risks: A disappointing outlook while it trades below its 200-day average.

targets.name: Humana
targets.thesis: Its Medicare Advantage business is recovering after a favorable rate notice; the stock is at a 52-week high with steady momentum.
targets.risks: Medical costs could rise or star ratings could slip.

targets.name: Illumina, Inc.
targets.thesis: Q3 beat estimates and the company raised guidance; the 23% pullback looks like profit-taking, and the November 17 Jefferies talk is a near-term catalyst.
targets.risks: China exposure and high volatility could extend the pullback.

fill_rule: the Interactive Brokers demo account's fills at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday, 16:00 New York); if the broker cannot be reached, simulated at that day's Lang & Schwarz session end, mid +/- 0.05%
rules: Paper money: $100,000 at the start, in US dollars.
Only S&P 500 companies; 10 to 15 of them.
At most 10% in one company, at least 3% in each one held; cash up to 20%.
At most 3 companies in or out per decision.
Claude decides twice a week: Wednesday evening and Saturday morning.
Orders go to an Interactive Brokers demo account and fill at the US closing auction (Thursday or Monday); the site records those fills: same shares, same prices.
Whole shares only, as at the broker.
Interactive Brokers' commission on each order ($1 when a fill has to be simulated); results shown before tax and after a 26% tax if sold.
No short selling, no leverage, no options, no crypto.
